payload.prompt: What is the Azure Language SDK?

options.text: A client library for Azure Language features
options.rationale: This is ready-made developer code for adding Azure Language capabilities to an application. It supports features such as language detection and PII redaction.

options.text: A library for deployed OpenAI models
options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language SDK with OpenAI Python library
options.rationale: This describes the OpenAI Python library, which interacts with OpenAI models and services. It is not the Azure Language client library.
options.better_fit: Choose this when Python code must interact with OpenAI models and services.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing this would focus the developer on model access instead of the purpose-built language features needed.
feedback.instructional: Keep the libraries separate: Azure Language SDK is for Azure Language capabilities, while the OpenAI Python library connects to OpenAI models.

options.error_type: Confuses SDK with a model
options.rationale: A general-purpose model follows prompts and can handle many language tasks. An SDK is ready-made code used to call capabilities from an application.
options.better_fit: Choose this for flexible, prompt-based analysis such as summarizing or answering questions.

feedback.intrinsic: This choice would not identify the code library needed to add language detection or PII redaction.
feedback.instructional: A model analyzes language; the Azure Language SDK is the client library that lets an application use Azure Language features.

options.error_type: Confuses client library with portal
options.rationale: The portal is a web interface for building, testing, and deploying applications. The SDK is used in application code.
options.better_fit: Choose this when referring to the web interface used to build, test, and deploy applications.

feedback.intrinsic: This would send someone to a browser interface when the task calls for code integration.
feedback.instructional: Use the portal to explore and manage work; use the Azure Language SDK inside an application.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Azure Language SDK is a client library that adds Azure Language capabilities to applications.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: The Azure Language SDK can add language detection and PII redaction to an application.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. These are Azure Language capabilities that the SDK can add to an application.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice would overlook two key capabilities available through the library.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The Azure Language SDK supports language detection and PII detection with redaction.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: The Azure Language SDK is installed with pip install openai.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. That command installs a different library.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Using that package name would install the OpenAI Python library instead of the Azure Language SDK.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Install the Azure Language Python SDK with pip install azure-ai-textanalytics.

payload.prompt: Complete the installation command.
payload.explanation: The Azure Language Python SDK is distributed under the azure-ai-textanalytics package name. The openai package is for the separate OpenAI Python library.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That package would not give the application the Azure Language Python SDK.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use azure-ai-textanalytics. Do not confuse it with openai, which installs the separate OpenAI Python library.

payload.prompt: A support-app developer must detect each ticket's language and redact personal details before the ticket is shared. Which library should the developer choose?

options.rationale: This library adds language detection and PII redaction to applications. Those capabilities match both requirements in the scenario.

options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language SDK with OpenAI library
options.rationale: This library is for Python applications that interact with OpenAI models and services. It is not the purpose-built Azure Language library for fixed language detection and PII methods.
options.better_fit: Choose this when code needs to send requests to OpenAI models and services.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would not be using the purpose-built methods intended for language routing and redaction.
feedback.instructional: For language detection and PII redaction in an application, choose the Azure Language SDK.

options.error_type: Confuses SDK with API for general-purpose models
options.rationale: The Responses API sends natural-language prompts to a deployed model. It is intended for flexible conversational-style analysis rather than fixed Azure Language methods.
options.better_fit: Choose this for flexible prompt-based analysis with a deployed language model.

feedback.intrinsic: Results could vary in wording or formatting when the workflow needs consistent language and redaction results.
feedback.instructional: Use the Azure Language SDK when the application needs purpose-built language detection and PII redaction.

options.error_type: Confuses application library with testing interface
options.rationale: The playground lets people explore capabilities in the portal. It does not add those capabilities to application code.
options.better_fit: Choose this when testing or exploring capabilities in the Foundry portal.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer could test a capability but would still not have it integrated into the support application.
feedback.instructional: Use the SDK for application code; use the playground for exploration.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Azure Language SDK provides purpose-built language detection and PII redaction for applications.

payload.prompt: A bank processes loan applications. Its automated workflow needs fixed language codes and redacted text before files are reviewed. Which choice fits best?

options.rationale: The SDK provides purpose-built methods for language detection and PII redaction. These methods return consistent, structured values needed by an automated workflow.

options.error_type: Confuses predictable Azure Language analysis with general model access
options.rationale: This library gives Python code access to OpenAI models and services. General model responses can vary between calls.
options.better_fit: Choose this when an application needs to interact with OpenAI models and services.

feedback.intrinsic: The bank may receive slightly different wording or formatting where fixed values are needed before review.
feedback.instructional: For consistent language codes and redacted text, use the purpose-built Azure Language SDK.

options.error_type: Confuses structured Azure Language results with flexible prompts
options.rationale: The Responses API supports complete interactions with deployed language models. Its prompt-driven output is flexible rather than fixed structured Azure Language output.
options.better_fit: Choose this for conversational-style analysis that can be expressed through natural-language prompts.

feedback.intrinsic: A prompt-based response may not provide the consistent values required by the automated review flow.
feedback.instructional: Use Azure Language methods when the workflow requires a language code, confidence score, or redacted text.

options.error_type: Confuses testing in a portal with application integration
options.rationale: The playground is for testing Azure Language capabilities in the portal. It does not provide the code integration needed for automated processing.
options.better_fit: Choose this when exploring Azure Language capabilities before building an application.

feedback.intrinsic: The bank could test a feature but could not process its applications automatically from the playground.
feedback.instructional: Use the SDK in application code for the automated workflow.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The SDK fits workflows that need consistent language details and redacted text.

payload.prompt: Which statements describe AzureKeyCredential and TextAnalyticsClient? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: AzureKeyCredential provides API-key credentials for authenticated Azure SDK access. It supplies the key when creating the client.

options.text: TextAnalyticsClient is an Azure Language client
options.rationale: TextAnalyticsClient is the Python client for Azure Language text analysis. Its methods call Azure Language capabilities.

options.text: TextAnalyticsClient is a deployed model name
options.error_type: Confuses client object with model deployment
options.rationale: TextAnalyticsClient is a client class used for Azure Language analysis. A deployment name identifies a deployed general-purpose model.
options.better_fit: Choose this description for the name assigned to a deployed general-purpose model.

feedback.intrinsic: A developer would look for a model deployment instead of creating the Azure Language client needed to make requests.
feedback.instructional: TextAnalyticsClient is the client; a deployment name identifies a deployed general-purpose model.

options.error_type: Confuses credential with analysis method
options.rationale: AzureKeyCredential supplies an API key for authenticated access. It does not perform any text analysis.
options.better_fit: Choose this for detect_language(), which detects language details.

feedback.intrinsic: The application would have credentials but would not make a language-detection request.
feedback.instructional: Use AzureKeyCredential for access and detect_language() for language analysis.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. AzureKeyCredential provides access credentials, and TextAnalyticsClient calls Azure Language capabilities.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: TextAnalyticsClient can be created with an endpoint and AzureKeyCredential(key).
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The client is configured with the Azure Language endpoint and an API-key credential.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Without both parts, the client configuration described here is incomplete.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Create TextAnalyticsClient with the endpoint and AzureKeyCredential(key).

payload.prompt: Order the pieces correctly.
payload.explanation: The endpoint identifies where the client connects, while AzureKeyCredential(key) provides authenticated access. Both are used when creating TextAnalyticsClient.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The configuration roles become unclear when the client, endpoint, and credential are out of sequence.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the client first, then connect its endpoint and API-key credential to the access purpose.

payload.prompt: A developer is building an app to analyze customer notes with Azure Language. The app must create an authenticated Azure Language client. Which code pieces are needed? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: TextAnalyticsClient is the Azure Language Python client. It is the client created to call language-analysis methods.
AzureKeyCredential(key) supplies the API key for authenticated access. It is passed as the credential when creating the client.
This environment variable holds the Azure Language endpoint. The endpoint is used to configure the client connection.

options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language client with OpenAI model deployment
options.rationale: A model deployment name is used when calling a deployed general-purpose model with the OpenAI API. TextAnalyticsClient does not use it in the shown configuration.
options.better_fit: Choose this when calling a deployed model through the OpenAI API.

feedback.intrinsic: Including this name would not complete the Azure Language client configuration.
feedback.instructional: For this client, use the Azure Language endpoint and AzureKeyCredential(key), not a model deployment name.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The client needs TextAnalyticsClient, its Azure Language endpoint, and an API-key credential.

payload.prompt: Which method detects the language of text?

options.rationale: detect_language() evaluates text to identify its primary language. It also returns the ISO 639-1 code and confidence score.

options.error_type: Confuses language detection with PII detection
options.rationale: recognize_pii_entities() finds personal details and returns redacted text plus entity details. It does not return primary-language details.
options.better_fit: Choose this when identifying and redacting personally identifiable information.

feedback.intrinsic: The request would look for personal details instead of producing the language information needed.
feedback.instructional: Use detect_language() for language name, ISO code, and confidence; use recognize_pii_entities() for PII.

options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language method with OpenAI API method
options.rationale: responses.create() sends a natural-language prompt to a deployed language model. It is not the Azure Language SDK method that returns fixed language-detection fields.
options.better_fit: Choose this when sending prompts to a deployed language model for flexible analysis.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would need to design a prompt rather than receive the stated language-detection result directly.
feedback.instructional: For the purpose-built detection call, use detect_language().

options.error_type: Confuses analysis method with credential object
options.rationale: AzureKeyCredential() creates an API-key credential. It does not analyze a string or return a language.
options.better_fit: Choose this when supplying an API key while creating an Azure SDK client.

feedback.intrinsic: The application could authenticate but would not detect the message language.
feedback.instructional: Credentials provide access; detect_language() performs the language analysis.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. detect_language() returns the primary language details for supplied text.

payload.prompt: What does detect_language() return for a text string? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The result includes the primary language name. Code can read it from primary_language.name.
The result includes the language's ISO 639-1 code. Code can read it from primary_language.iso6391_name.
The result includes a confidence score between 0 and 1. This shows confidence in the detected language.

options.error_type: Confuses language detection with PII detection
options.rationale: Redacted text is returned by PII detection. Language detection returns language details and confidence instead.
options.better_fit: Choose this for recognize_pii_entities(), which returns a redacted version of the input.

feedback.intrinsic: Selecting this would mix privacy output with language-routing output.
feedback.instructional: Keep the methods distinct: detect_language() returns language details; recognize_pii_entities() returns redacted text.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The method returns a language name, ISO 639-1 code, and confidence score.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: detect_language() returns redacted text and PII entity categories.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Those results belong to PII detection, not language detection.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would mix the results used for privacy handling with the results used for language routing.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: detect_language() returns language name, ISO 639-1 code, and confidence score. recognize_pii_entities() returns redacted text and PII details.

payload.prompt: Complete the method call that passes one text string as a list.
payload.explanation: detect_language() accepts a list of strings, so [text] passes one string in the required list form. The final [0] accesses the first returned result.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Using the PII method here would produce privacy-related results instead of a detected language.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use detect_language([text]) when the goal is language identification. recognize_pii_entities([text]) is for personal-detail detection.

payload.prompt: A support-team developer needs each incoming customer message routed by language name, ISO code, and confidence score. Which method should the developer call?

options.rationale: This method returns the detected language name, ISO 639-1 code, and confidence score. Those fields support routing by language.

options.error_type: Confuses language detection with PII detection
options.rationale: This method identifies personal details and returns redacted text with entity information. It does not supply language-routing fields.
options.better_fit: Choose this when messages need personal details identified or redacted.

feedback.intrinsic: Messages could be prepared for privacy sharing but could not be routed from their language details.
feedback.instructional: Use detect_language() when routing depends on language name, ISO code, and confidence.

options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language SDK with OpenAI API
options.rationale: This call sends prompts to a deployed language model. It does not directly return the fixed language-detection fields described here.
options.better_fit: Choose this for flexible prompt-based analysis with a deployed language model.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would need a prompt and could receive variable formatting instead of the required routing fields.
feedback.instructional: For consistent language details, call detect_language().

options.error_type: Confuses request method with credential
options.rationale: This creates the credential used for authenticated access. It does not send a message for analysis.
options.better_fit: Choose this when creating an authenticated Azure Language client.

feedback.intrinsic: The application could have a key but would not produce routing information.
feedback.instructional: Use AzureKeyCredential(key) to create the client, then use detect_language() to analyze a message.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. detect_language() provides exactly the language name, ISO code, and confidence information needed for routing.

payload.prompt: What can recognize_pii_entities() return? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The result contains a redacted version of the input. This supports sharing content after personal details are hidden.
Each detected entity includes its text. This lets code report what was found.
Each entity includes a category and confidence score. These details describe the detected personal information.

options.error_type: Confuses PII detection with language detection
options.rationale: A primary language ISO code comes from language detection. PII detection instead returns redacted text and entity details.
options.better_fit: Choose this for detect_language(), which returns the ISO 639-1 code.

feedback.intrinsic: This would confuse a privacy result with a value used to identify and route languages.
feedback.instructional: Use recognize_pii_entities() for redaction and entity details; use detect_language() for the primary-language ISO code.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. PII detection returns redacted content and details about the personal entities it finds.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: recognize_pii_entities() identifies personal details and can return redacted text.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The method identifies PII and provides a redacted result along with entity details.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would leave out the method's key privacy purpose.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: recognize_pii_entities() identifies personal details and returns redacted text plus information about detected entities.

payload.prompt: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.
payload.explanation: PII detection has two useful outputs: content with personal details redacted and records describing the entities found. The order links the method to both outputs clearly.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A mixed-up sentence can hide the important link between redaction and the detected-entity details.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the method, then state that it provides redacted content plus PII entities with details.

payload.prompt: A healthcare system must share a medical note after hiding personal details, while also logging what was found. Which PII results should its developer use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is the version with detected PII redacted. It is appropriate for sharing after personal details are hidden.
This identifies the category of each detected entity. It supports logging what kind of personal detail was found.
This gives the confidence score for each detected entity. It supports logging the returned entity information.

options.error_type: Confuses PII result with language result
options.rationale: This property is read from a language-detection result. It does not provide the redacted content or PII entity details required here.
options.better_fit: Choose this after detect_language() when logging a primary language ISO code.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could record a language code but would not have the privacy results needed for sharing and logging.
feedback.instructional: For PII handling, use redacted_text and each entity's category and confidence score.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. These properties support both a shareable redacted note and a record of detected PII.

payload.prompt: What is MCP?

options.text: An open standard for agent tool connections
options.rationale: MCP defines a standard way for agents to connect to external capabilities and data sources. It avoids custom integration code for every service.

options.text: A Python library for Azure Language
options.error_type: Confuses protocol with SDK
options.rationale: The Azure Language SDK is a Python client library. MCP is an open connection standard for agents and external capabilities.
options.better_fit: Choose this description for the Azure Language SDK.

feedback.intrinsic: This would lead someone to look for application code instead of a standard connection approach for agents.
feedback.instructional: MCP is a protocol, while the Azure Language SDK is a client library.

options.text: A client object for text analysis
options.error_type: Confuses protocol with client object
options.rationale: A client object is a specific object created to call a service. MCP defines how clients and servers communicate.
options.better_fit: Choose this for TextAnalyticsClient, the Azure Language Python client.

feedback.intrinsic: The roles in a client-server connection would remain unclear.
feedback.instructional: MCP is the shared protocol; TextAnalyticsClient is a client used for Azure Language analysis.

options.error_type: Confuses protocol with model deployment
options.rationale: A deployment name identifies a deployed general-purpose model. MCP is unrelated to naming a model deployment.
options.better_fit: Choose this when referring to the name assigned during deployment of a general-purpose model.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would name a model rather than establish the shared connection approach it needs.
feedback.instructional: MCP connects agents with external capabilities; a deployment name identifies a deployed model.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. MCP is an open standard that lets agents connect to external capabilities and data sources.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: MCP requires custom integration code for every external service an agent uses.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. MCP provides a standard connection approach instead of custom integration for every service.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That approach would recreate the per-service work MCP is intended to avoid.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: MCP acts like a universal adapter: an agent can connect to an MCP server that exposes capabilities in a standard way.

payload.prompt: Complete the term: the open standard that connects agents to external tools and data sources is ____.
payload.explanation: MCP means Model Context Protocol and defines a common connection method for agents and external capabilities. An API and the Azure Language SDK are related technologies, but neither is this open standard.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing a related term would not identify the standard that avoids custom integration for every service.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use MCP or Model Context Protocol. An API defines software communication rules, and the Azure Language SDK is a client library.

payload.prompt: Put the pieces in the correct order.
payload.explanation: MCP standardizes connections between agents and external capabilities. That standardization removes the need to write separate integration code for every service.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The main benefit of MCP is harder to understand when the connection and reduced-code ideas are separated.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Put the connection idea first, then show that it avoids custom code for every service.

payload.prompt: A legal-services team is building an agent to use several external tools for case files. The team wants one standard connection approach instead of custom code for every service. What should they use?

options.rationale: MCP is the open standard for connecting agents to external capabilities and data sources. It avoids custom integration work for every service.

options.text: A custom API integration per service
options.error_type: Misses MCP standardization benefit
options.rationale: This means writing separate integration code for every service. That is the repeated work MCP is designed to avoid.
options.better_fit: Choose this when a needed service does not provide the required standard connection.

feedback.intrinsic: The legal team would have to maintain separate connections as it adds services.
feedback.instructional: When several services are involved, MCP provides the shared connection approach.

options.error_type: Confuses authentication credential with connection protocol
options.rationale: AzureKeyCredential supplies an API key for authenticated Azure SDK access. It does not define how agents connect to several external services.
options.better_fit: Choose this when creating an Azure SDK client that authenticates with an API key.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could supply a key for one client but would still lack the shared agent connection method.
feedback.instructional: A credential proves authorized access; MCP standardizes the agent's connection to external capabilities.

options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language client with agent protocol
options.rationale: TextAnalyticsClient is a Python client for Azure Language analysis. It is not a common protocol for connecting an agent to several services.
options.better_fit: Choose this in application code that calls Azure Language methods directly.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would gain one language-analysis client but not the common approach needed for multiple services.
feedback.instructional: Use MCP for the shared agent connection approach; TextAnalyticsClient is for direct Azure Language application code.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. MCP is the standard connection approach for agents that need multiple external capabilities.

payload.prompt: An AI agent is connected to an Azure Language MCP server to analyze customer feedback. Which statements correctly describe this connection? Select all that apply.

options.text: The agent can be the MCP client
options.rationale: An AI agent, or the host application running it, can be the MCP client. The client sends requests and receives responses.

options.text: The client sends requests and receives responses
options.rationale: Sending requests and receiving responses is the client's role. This can be the agent or host application.

options.text: The server exposes tools or data
options.rationale: The MCP server exposes capabilities, data, or actions. It runs the requested capability and returns a structured result.

options.text: The client must expose server tools
options.error_type: Reverses MCP client and server roles
options.rationale: The server exposes capabilities for the client to discover and invoke. The client sends requests rather than exposing the server's capabilities.
options.better_fit: Choose this description for the MCP server, which exposes tools, data, or actions.

feedback.intrinsic: Reversing the roles would make it unclear where the agent should send its request.
feedback.instructional: Remember the direction: client requests; server exposes capabilities and returns structured results.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. In MCP, the client requests capabilities and the server exposes them and returns structured results.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: The managed Azure Language MCP server exposes Azure Language features through MCP.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. It bridges an agent to Azure Language capabilities through the MCP standard.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would miss how an agent reaches managed Azure Language capabilities through MCP.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The managed Azure Language MCP server exposes Azure Language features, including named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and language detection.

payload.prompt: Arrange the following steps in MCP request order.
payload.explanation: The client initiates the exchange by sending a request. The server receives it, runs the relevant capability, and returns a structured result.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An out-of-order flow would make the response appear before the server has handled the request.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the client-server sequence: request, receipt, capability execution, then structured result.

payload.prompt: Complete the term: the managed service that exposes Azure Language features through MCP is the ____.
payload.explanation: The Azure Language MCP server is the managed bridge that exposes Azure Language capabilities through MCP. The SDK and TextAnalyticsClient are used in application code, while the MCP client sends requests.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing a related component would assign the server's role to the wrong part of the connection.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use Azure Language MCP server. The SDK and TextAnalyticsClient are clients for application code, and the MCP client sends requests.

payload.prompt: A customer-support lead wants a Foundry agent to route tickets by language and redact PII. What should the team do? Select all that apply.

options.text: Add Azure Language MCP server as a tool
options.rationale: Adding this server connects the agent to Azure Language capabilities through MCP. It can support language routing and PII redaction.

options.text: Configure it with the Foundry resource name

options.text: Prompt the agent to use the connected tool
options.rationale: Prompts can instruct the agent to analyze content using the connected capability. This combines the model's reasoning with Azure Language's predictable analysis.

options.text: Create a separate Azure Language resource

options.rationale: A Foundry resource provides a unified environment that already includes access to Language capabilities. A separate Azure Language resource is not needed for this connection.
options.better_fit: Choose this only when working outside the stated Foundry resource workflow.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would add unnecessary setup before it could connect the agent.
feedback.instructional: Use the existing Foundry resource name to configure the Azure Language MCP server; no separate Azure Language resource is required.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Connect the Azure Language MCP server with the Foundry resource name and instruct the agent to use it for language routing and PII redaction.

payload.prompt: A healthcare organization wants its Foundry agent to get predictable language analysis and PII redaction without direct REST calls or token handling. Which choices fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The managed server exposes Azure Language capabilities through MCP. It lets the agent use predictable language analysis and PII redaction.
The Foundry resource name configures the connection to the managed Azure Language MCP server. The unified resource includes access to Language capabilities.

options.text: Instruct the agent to use its tool
options.rationale: Prompts can direct the agent to analyze content with its connected capability. This lets the agent combine reasoning with Azure Language analysis.

options.text: Call Azure Language REST API directly
options.error_type: Bypasses managed MCP server
options.rationale: The managed Azure Language MCP server avoids direct REST API calls and authentication-token management in agent code. Calling REST directly bypasses the stated approach.
options.better_fit: Choose this when building an integration without the managed MCP server.

feedback.intrinsic: The organization would take on direct integration and authentication work that the managed connection avoids.
feedback.instructional: Connect the Azure Language MCP server instead; it exposes the capabilities through MCP without direct REST calls or token handling.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The managed MCP connection uses the Foundry resource name and prompts to give the agent predictable Azure Language analysis.
